title: Tenant isolation: throughput, latency, and cost snapshot (multi-tenant vs isolated)
content:
Summary:

This is a compact draft of an internal snapshot comparing multi-tenant (shared-GPU, cgroup-based) vs isolated (pinned-instance) serving configurations. Purpose: produce a short, evidence-backed recommendation for capacity planning and SLO pricing tradeoffs for mid-market customers. This focuses on throughput scalability, p50/p95/p99 latency, jitter during background interference, and an estimated cost-per-1000-tokens model under each mode.

Experiment setup (concise):
- Date: 2026-03-15 to 2026-03-18 (runs repeated across 3 days to capture noise).
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 40GB (hosted nodes), identical kernel and driver stack, runtime v0.9.8.
- Configs tested:
  * Multi-tenant-shared (MTS): 4 customers multiplexed on one instance using cgroups + runtime slotting; kernel preemption on; no static reservation.
  * Isolated-pinned (IP): single tenant pinned to the GPU instance with dedicated executor and KV cache pinned; no other work.
- Models: small/medium transformer (redwood-medium-13B-q4), sequence length 512 prompt + 512 gen, typical chat-turn pattern.
- Workload profiles:
  * Steady low-rate: 10 qps, 90% short (50 tokens), 10% long (500 tokens)
  * Bursty (microburst): sustained 80 qps for 10s every 2 minutes
  * Background interference: concurrent offline batch embedding jobs injected at 10%/30%/60% GPU utilization
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency (token-first and total), tail-jitter (p99.9-p95), throughput (tokens/s), KV cache hit rate, and cost estimate (cost model described below).

Raw result highlights (median across runs):
- Steady low-rate:
  * IP: p50=45ms/token, p95=62ms/token, p99=160ms/token, throughput headroom ~120%
  * MTS: p50=48ms/token, p95=78ms/token, p99=340ms/token, throughput headroom ~85%
- Bursty period (during 10s spikes):
  * IP: p95 rises to 120ms/token, p99=220ms/token, observed graceful queueing, no cross-tenant amplification
  * MTS: p95 spikes to 290ms/token, p99 frequently > 900ms/token (observed queuing + kernel-level preemption thrash)
- Background interference (30% batch load):
  * IP: tail latency increases modestly (p95 +30%), throughput steady
  * MTS: tail latency increases dramatically (p95 +120%, p99 +300%), jitter increases (p99.9-p95 goes from ~60ms to ~420ms)

Text chart: p95 latency comparison (steady / burst / bg-interfere) in ms (median)

Mode     | Steady | Burst  | Bg-30%
---------|--------|--------|--------
Isolated | 62     | 120    | 80
Shared   | 78     | 290    | 170

Tail jitter (p99.9 - p95) in ms

Mode     | Steady | Bg-30%
---------|--------|--------
Isolated | 60     | 120
Shared   | 60     | 420

Throughput headroom (relative to steady target)

Mode     | Headroom
---------|---------
Isolated | +120%
Shared   | +85%

Cost model (approx):
- Baseline infra cost per GPU-hour (hosted price): $3.20/hr (amortized)
- Effective user throughput considered: tokens/s observed under each scenario
- Example normalized number: for the tested workload, IP achieved 1.9M tokens/hr; MTS delivered 1.3M tokens/hr per tenant (due to interference and conservative admission).
- Estimated cost/1k tokens (infrastructure only): IP ~ $0.0017 / 1k tokens; MTS ~ $0.0025 / 1k tokens (tenant-level QoS overhead + throughput loss).

Interpretation and analysis:
- Multi-tenant sharing looks attractive for average-case cost if you only care about p50/p95; however, under bursty traffic and background batch interference it suffers from large tail amplifications. That leads to actual SLO misses for conversational workloads that are sensitive to tail latency.
- Isolated instances provide tighter tail control and much better headroom, reducing the need for conservative admission controls. The cost-per-token advantage flips once you factor in the business cost of SLO misses (retries, UX degradation, SLA credits).
- The dominant failure mode in MTS is kernel/GPU preemption interactions during memory pressure and KV-cache eviction churn. We saw repeated cache thrashing when two tenants simultaneously hit long-sequence generation.

Observability notes (what to add to the console):
- Add tenant-level jitter metric (p95 vs p99.9 gap) surfaced on per-route dashboards.
- Surface "interference score": correlation of background batch GPU utilization with p99 latency per tenant over last 1h.
- Per-tenant admission heuristics should include a flag for "strict-tail" customers (A/B pricing to isolate).

Recommendation (short):
- For customers with strict tail SLOs (p99 < 500ms per token target), prefer isolated/pinned instances and price accordingly.
- For best-effort customers, consider MTS but enforce scheduled batch windows and stricter background job isolation.
- Product: add an option in Dedicated/Dashboard to opt-in for "tenant-isolation = strict" which will map to isolated capacity with a higher price.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Repeat with larger model family (redwood-large-70B-quant) to confirm scaling of cache thrash behavior.
- Test with different scheduler knobs: kernel preemption off, cgroup cpu shares adjusted, runtime slot-size variations (ticket: JIRA-RED-8421 follow-ups).
- Validate cost model across cloud regions (we only tested us-west).

Quick next steps:
1) Run 2-day validation on redwood-large with the same interference patterns (owner: Samir).
2) Wire an "interference score" metric prototype into the internal dashboard (owner: Evelyn).
3) Draft short product brief proposing the isolation opt-in and differential pricing (owner: Jordan).

Notes to reviewers: this is a working snapshot — numbers are median-of-medians across runs and intentionally conservative. Expect variance +/- 10-25% for p95 and throughput in cross-day runs. Attachments: raw CSVs in the benchmark S3 bucket (see confluence page link above).

Unresolved: whether we can reduce MTS tail via runtime-level KV-cache pinning per tenant (requires kernel cgroup changes + runtime work - see PR linked above).

End of snapshot.
